newsitem.title: USA: Spreads on U.S. interest rate swaps hardly budge.
newsitem.headline: Spreads on U.S. interest rate swaps hardly budge.

text.p: U.S. interest rate swaps remained locked in place this week, despite the market's revised outlook for short-term rates, dealers said.

Following Tuesday's surprise decision by Federal Reserve Board's Open Market Committee to leave short-term rates unchanged, spreads on swaps moved only a few basis points and stayed well within their recent trading ranges.
"It was really a blip, which may show that people didn't have any big trades on in swaps by the time (the Fed) made a decision," one dealer in New York said.
Expectations for short-term interest rates as seen in Eurodollar futures have dropped by about 20 basis points since the Fed meeting.

The December euro contract shows moderating expectations of tightening, for example. The contract has gained 19 basis points since Tuesday to an implied yield of 5.75 percent, with current three-month LIBOR at 5.44 percent. The March 1997 contract gained 21 basis points to 5.88 percent and the June contract gained the same to yield 6.05 percent.
Spreads on two-year LIBOR swaps tightened by one to two basis points after the Fed meeting, but have since widened.

On Thursday, spreads were quoted at 17 basis points bid, 19 to 20 basis points offered. Spreads were just a few basis points wider back in June, several Fed meetings ago, one New York-based trader noted.
Quotes on three-year swaps fluctuated a bit after this week's meeting, but then settled into almost unchanged levels.
Spreads on three-year LIBOR swaps were quoted at 19 basis points bid, 21 basis points offered on Thursday.
At the longer end, from five to 10 years, swap spreads were seen slightly tighter on the offer side, dealer said.
Dealers were seen trying to entice fixed-rate payers into the market with the lower offer-side quotes.

On five-year swaps, spreads were quoted at 24 basis points bid, 26 basis points offered, about one basis point tighter on the offer side than before the Fed meeting. The upcoming auction of five-year notes had no impact on spreads, dealers said.
On 10-year swaps, spreads were quoted at 33 basis points bid, 34 to 35 basis points offered, also slightly tighter on the offer.
